candidate.title: Privilege escalation to ALLOW_ADMIN: non-admin user registers an ALLOW_ADMIN session key, then ADMIN_SET grants ALLOW_WITHDRAW on any victim account and drains it

ice.impact: Attacker withdraws the victim account's full collateral balance to an attacker-controlled address.
ice.exploit_path: REGISTER_ACCOUNT (self-mint ALLOW_ADMIN session key) -> ADMIN_SET_SIGNER_PERMISSIONS (grant ALLOW_WITHDRAW on victim via caller-named adminAccountId) -> WITHDRAWAL (drain victim)

evidence.attacker_model: Drain any victim account's collateral by granting the attacker's session key ALLOW_WITHDRAW on the victim, after self-minting ALLOW_ADMIN.
evidence.preconditions: REGISTER_ACCOUNT (self-mint ALLOW_ADMIN session key) -> ADMIN_SET_SIGNER_PERMISSIONS (grant ALLOW_WITHDRAW on victim via caller-named adminAccountId) -> WITHDRAWAL (drain victim)
evidence.who_loses: Any account holder whose collateral is drained
evidence.who_gains: Unprivileged attacker (registers an account, self-grants ALLOW_ADMIN)
evidence.impact: Any user can mint themselves ALLOW_ADMIN at registration and, because processAdminSetSignerPermissions trusts the caller's adminAccountId, grant ALLOW_WITHDRAW/ALLOW_TRANSFER (or ALLOW_ADMIN) on ANY victim account and drain it. Total loss of the protocol's permission model and user funds — bounded on-chain only by the trusted txBatcher/backend declining to relay the txs. There is no on-chain check enforcing that adminAccountId == SignerManager.adminAccountId(), and no delegation gate on registration-time session-key masks.
evidence.suggested_fix: Bind processAdminSetSignerPermissions to canonical SignerManager.adminAccountId(); apply the owner-holds-the-bit delegation gate to registration-time signer masks (or strip ALLOW_ADMIN at registration).
